global_issue_check_order: For each new ticket, first search for an open global ticket matching the same diagnosis/category, configuration item and location scope.
If a matching open global ticket exists, link the new ticket and tell the user it is a known issue; avoid duplicate individual diagnosis unless new evidence suggests a different cause.
If none exists, count recent non-global, unlinked, non-final tickets in the same scope and UTC time window.
Only create a global ticket when both the numeric threshold and shared-scope evidence are met; link related tickets and notify the owning resolver group.

outage_thresholds.scope: Exact category + configuration_item_id + location_id; AND filters
outage_thresholds.severity_selection: SEV1 only for confirmed critical business impact with human review; otherwise SEV2 for corroborated multi-user outage. Ticket count alone does not set severity.

scope_requirements: All tickets in a cluster must share the same canonical category, configuration item and location for the current mock backend's global-ticket API.
Do not create a global ticket if configuration_item_id or location_id is missing; send to human triage and document the missing scope.
The current backend count filters combine with AND and global-ticket creation requires category + CI + location. This policy is deliberately compatible with that constraint.
decoy_safeguards: Do not escalate based on category similarity alone.
Do not aggregate tickets across different locations or configuration items.
Do not aggregate reports outside the configured time window.
Require corroborating evidence: shared CI/location, close timestamps, and either degraded/unavailable service health or repeated consistent symptoms.
Run a negative control for the three decoy patterns: same category spread across days or different sites must not meet thresholds.

SEV1.definition: Confirmed critical business impact; requires human review. A burst count alone does not establish SEV1.
notify: GRP-INFRA when infrastructure dependency is plausible
SEV1.response: Create only a corroborated, correctly scoped global incident; initial owner must be GRP-L1. L1 coordinates human incident leadership. No autonomous remediation.

SEV2.definition: At least 3 eligible tickets in 30 minutes in one configured exact scope, plus corroborated multi-user service impact, without confirmed critical impact.
SEV2.response: Create/link global ticket, notify owner group, track affected tickets, update users with known-issue status.

SEV3.definition: Limited degradation, below-threshold pattern, uncertain scope, or a scope without a configured threshold; human review and further evidence collection.
SEV3.response: Continue evidence collection and human review; do not create a global ticket solely on weak similarity.

always_human_conditions: security_sensitive=true or suspected phishing, malware, account lock due to security policy, or suspected data exposure
evidence conflicts or diagnosis remains inconclusive after targeted questions/checks
destructive, irreversible, production-changing, certificate, shared storage, server, or account lifecycle action requiring approval
identity verification failure or any request to bypass MFA/security controls

confidence_policy.HIGH: Only when article match is strong, all required evidence is complete, similar-ticket evidence is supportive when available, and plausible competing diagnoses have been excluded. For HIGH specialist routing, follow backend review requirements.
confidence_policy.MEDIUM: Some evidence supports the diagnosis, but a non-safety gap remains. Assign GRP-L1 and attach recommended specialist group and rationale.
confidence_policy.LOW: Insufficient/conflicting evidence or multiple unresolved candidates. Do not force diagnosis; send to human triage or ask a discriminating question.

decoy_validation.decoy_1: Same category across multiple days: must not trigger.
decoy_validation.decoy_2: Same category at different sites: must not trigger.
decoy_validation.decoy_3: Similar descriptions but different configuration items: must not trigger.

backend_compatibility_notes: Source reviewed: outputs/workstream-c/data/escalation_policy.json, app/services.py, app/schemas.py, app/dataset.py and agent OpenAPI. This confirms supplied source behavior, not a running deployment.
Only VPN + CI-VPN + LOC-A, Availability + CI-PORTAL + LOC-B, and Availability + CI-ERP + LOC-C have configured numeric triggers: 3 tickets / 30 minutes. Do not generalize thresholds to other scopes.
The agent evaluates thresholds. The backend does not automatically evaluate counts or prove an outage.
Counts exclude global, linked, resolved and closed records; UTC window boundaries are inclusive. Use the backend demo clock or an explicit as_of consistent with fixture dates.
Creation requires category + CI + location; missing scope requires human triage. Check existing globals using the full known exact scope first.
Notifications are mock group records. A human incident lead is coordinated through L1.
Backend knowledge search excludes unapproved articles. All revised articles remain approved=false.

notification_policy.additional_recipients: Notify the diagnosed service owner group once. Add GRP-INFRA only for a plausible infrastructure dependency; GRP-SEC for security-sensitive evidence. Avoid unrelated group broadcasts.
notification_policy.SEV1: Notify L1 and relevant owner; L1 coordinates a human incident lead. The API accepts resolver group IDs, not a human incident lead recipient.
notification_policy.delivery: Notifications are MOCK records via notify_resolver_group, not email, chat or paging delivery.

global_ownership_rules: SEV1 global tickets initially belong to GRP-L1.
Any mandatory-human child requires GRP-L1 ownership of a new global ticket.
For ordinary SEV2 incidents, use the diagnosed service owner; use L1 when ownership is uncertain.
For existing globals, link without claiming severity or ownership was updated: creation reuses the current record without overwriting those facts.
